Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the GlobalBank Holdings Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up will be given at that time. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review GlobalBank Holdings's results for the Q3. With me this morning are Mike Chen, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; David Patel, Chief Risk Officer; Lisa Wong, Chief Credit Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Technology Officer; and Emily Carter, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Chen.

Mike Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. GlobalBank Holdings delivered exceptional results in the Q3, exceeding expectations and demonstrating the strength of our diversified business model.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on accelerating revenue growth, improving profitability, managing risk effectively, investing in technology and innovation, enhancing customer experience, strengthening our brand, and delivering value to our shareholders.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on our overall company performance. Ladies and gentlemen, we're thrilled with how we've performed this quarter. We delivered exceptional results that underscore the resilience and strategic execution of our franchise amid a dynamic macroeconomic environment—marked by the Federal Reserve's steady 5.25-5.50% fed funds rate, persistent inflation pressures, and intensifying competition from fintech disruptors. We not only exceeded our consensus estimates but also achieved record profitability, driven by disciplined expense management, robust balance sheet growth, and accelerated digital transformation initiatives.

Total revenue reached $14.2 billion, up 12% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter, surpassing our guidance midpoint by 300 basis points. This marks our ninth straight quarter of double-digit revenue growth, fueled by a 9% expansion in net interest income to $9.8 billion—reflecting NIM expansion to 3.72%, a 14 basis point improvement from Q2, as we optimized our loan-to-deposit ratio to 92% through higher-yielding commercial loans and a favorable deposit mix shift toward low-cost transaction accounts. Non-interest income, our growth engine, surged 22% to $4.4 billion, propelled by record fee income from payments processing—up 28%—and wealth management assets under management hitting $1.2 trillion, benefiting from equity market tailwinds.

On the bottom line, we reported net income available to common shareholders of $4.1 billion, a robust 15% increase YoY, translating to diluted EPS of $2.85—beating consensus by $0.22 and representing our highest quarterly figure ever. Return on tangible common equity expanded to 28.2%, well above our peer average of 22%, while our efficiency ratio improved to 52%, down 150 basis points YoY through expense synergies from our Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP migration and AI-driven back-office automation. Our CET1 capital ratio stands at 12.8% under Basel III endgame rules—positioning us for opportunistic share repurchases, with $3 billion deployed YTD—and tangible book value per share grew 8% to $42.50.

In commercial banking, revenues rose 16% to $6.4 billion on 11% loan growth to $450 billion, especially in middle-market C&I where we gained share in the Southeast U.S. Investment banking fees jumped 35% to $1.1 billion on M&A advisory and equity underwriting. Consumer banking saw 10% revenue growth to $5.2 billion, with deposits up 7% to $620 billion at low cost, thanks to our digital checking app adding primary relationships. Mortgage originations held at $25 billion with improved margins, and cards/payments volume up 18%. Wealth and investment management revenues grew 20% to $2.6 billion as AUM expanded 14%, with strong inflows into ETFs and our robo-advisor platform.

U.S. operations grew earnings 14%, with strength in high-growth MSAs. Internationally, Europe added 8% growth on cross-border deals, and Asia-Pacific saw 12% loan expansion in trade finance. Credit quality is pristine with net charge-offs at 22 bps, delinquencies at 0.9%, and ACL at 1.45%. We've invested heavily in tech, including core banking refresh on AWS for real-time payments and blockchain remittances.

Looking ahead, we're raising guidance: revenue growth to 11-13%, EPS to $11.40-$11.70, ROTE to 27-28%, with $15 billion for M&A and a dividend hike.

These results validate our digital first, customer centric framework. I'll now turn the call over to Sarah Thompson to discuss our financial results in more detail, including key strategic initiatives, non-interest income, efficiency, loans, and asset sensitivity.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Mike, and good morning. GlobalBank Holdings reported net income of $4.1 billion for the Q3, or $2.85 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 15% driven by higher loan yields and deposit growth. Non-interest income was up 12% year-over-year to $2.8 billion, reflecting strong performance in trading and wealth management.

Let me dive deeper into our key strategic initiatives and the progress we've made. Our strategy is anchored in three pillars: accelerating digital transformation, diversifying revenue streams through innovative products and partnerships, and fortifying our balance sheet amid a dynamic macroeconomic landscape. We've executed aggressively, delivering outcomes that position us for sustained growth.

Digital transformation now accounts for over 65% of operating investments, up from 45% two years ago. We've migrated 92% of core banking to hybrid cloud with AWS and Google Cloud, slashing time-to-market to under 90 days. Our GenAI-powered SmartAssist platform has driven 28% YoY mobile app engagement, with 14.2 million daily active users—72% of retail base. Fraud detection improved, reducing false positives by 35% and losses by $185 million YTD.

On APIs, we have 1,200+ live, partnering with Plaid for 4.5 million users and 22% uptick in embedded finance. In Europe, PSD2 unlocked £2.1 billion in payments, up 41%.

Revenue diversification: NII now 52% of revenue, down from 68%. Wealth & Asset Management AUM at $450 billion, up 19%, with GlobalWealth Pro adding 850,000 clients and $320 million fees. Payments via RippleNet processed $28 billion, up 55%.

North America: 61% revenues, 14% PPNR growth, consumer lending $45 billion. EMEA: UK acquisition added 2.1 million customers, CET1 13.2%. APAC: 32% revenue growth to $1.2 billion, BNPL with Grab, $8.5 billion green loans.

Risk management: loan-to-deposit 78%, diversified portfolio, LCR 145%. RegTech cut AML alerts 48%. ESG: $15 billion transition finance, green notes at 4.25%.

Progress: NPS 68, digital sales 82%, CIR 54.2% toward 50% target, cross-sell 4.2. Ahead: tokenization pilots, 15-18% ROE, NII $22-23 billion FY24.

Now, on the impact of market conditions on non-interest income, which totaled $2.8 billion, up 12% YoY and 5% QoQ, exceeding guidance. Resilient trading and wealth fees offset IB slowdown.

Investment banking fees $850 million, up 4% YoY, flat QoQ; high rates dampened M&A (global volume down 18%), but ECM strong with $15 billion underwritten, 8% share. Trading $1.1 billion, up 22% YoY on VIX 22 volatility; FICC $650 million, equities $450 million, prime $120 billion up 25%. Wealth fees $550 million, up 16%, AUM $1.2 trillion on $25 billion inflows. Service/card fees $300 million, up 5%.

Non-interest now 28% of revenue. AI algos, BlackRock partnership, APAC hub ahead.

Capital ratios strong. Now, on efficiency ratio progress: ours improved to 54.8% in Q3, down 110 bps QoQ and 420 bps YoY, YTD 55.4% ahead of 54-55% guide. TTM 55.2%, better than peers.

Expenses $2.85 billion, up 1.2% YoY, with $180 million UniCore savings automating workflows, AI assistant handling 72% inquiries. U.S. 52.1%, Europe 58.3% improving via branch closures. Revenue up 8.5% to $5.20 billion, NIM 3.45%.

FY24 target 54-55%, Q4 54.0-54.5%; sub-52% 2025, <50% 2027 via digital, diversification, optimization.

On loan growth by segment: average loans up 6.2% YoY, 1.8% QoQ to $285 billion. Commercial (52%, $148 billion) up 9.1% YoY: C&I 12%, CRE 6.5% with multifamily 14%. Tech underwriting, cross-sell.

Consumer (28%, $80 billion) up 4.3%: auto 7.2%, digital 45% originations. Mortgage (20%, $57 billion) up 1.8%, purchase focus, broker partnerships.

Balanced growth, guide 6-7%.

Finally, asset sensitivity: +$285 million for +100 bps, 3.8% of NII. Gap +12%, deposit beta 42%. EVE -4.2% +200 bps. Hedging $15 billion swaps, advanced modeling. Regional positioning: U.S. tailwind, Europe neutral, APAC adjusting. Ready for cuts.

Our capital ratios remain strong, well-positioned for growth.

I will now turn the call over to David Patel.

David Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. From a risk management perspective, we are closely monitoring geopolitical tensions, interest rate volatility, and commercial real estate exposure. We are taking proactive steps to mitigate these risks and maintain a strong risk profile, including stress-testing against 200bps shocks, maintaining LCR at 145%, and de-risking volatile segments well below peers.

Lisa Wong:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains exceptionally strong with non-performing loan ratio at 0.92%, down 15 bps QoQ and 28 bps YoY—lowest since 2019. Net charge-offs 42 bps annualized, down 10% QoQ, below peers. Delinquencies 1.85%, improved from 2.12%.

Trends broad-based: consumer 2.65% delinquencies, C&I NPLs 0.75%, mortgages 0.45%. U.S. drove improvements, EMEA slight rise but de-risked. Early Warning System 2.0 using AI reduced delinquencies 18%, tighter underwriting. Provisions $450 million, ACL 1.25% covering 170% NPLs. Q4 NPLs 0.90-1.00%, charge-offs 40-45 bps.

We are actively managing our loan portfolio and remain confident. Specifically, the performance of our commercial portfolio has been strong.

Raj Singh:
Thank you. I'd like to provide an update on our technology initiatives. We are making significant progress on our digital transformation, including the launch of SmartAssist which has seen 28% increase in engagement and $185 million fraud savings, plus API ecosystem and cloud migration driving efficiency gains.

Emily Carter:
Good morning. We are focused on operational excellence and driving efficiency across the organization. Key initiatives include UniCore platform migration and AI-powered customer service, which are contributing to improved productivity, $180 million savings, and efficiency ratio trending to 50%.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will open the lines for questions. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide further insights into your digital transformation progress and API initiatives?

Mike Chen:
Good morning, John. Absolutely, digital transformation is core, with 92% cloud migration reducing time-to-market to 90 days. SmartAssist has 14.2 million DAUs, and our 1,200 APIs with Plaid and PSD2 compliance are driving embedded finance and payments growth—22% uptick in revenues. This positions us competitively like JPMorgan.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez:
What are your plans for capital deployment and buybacks?

Sarah Thompson:
Thanks, Maria. With CET1 at 12.8-13.2%, we're deploying $3 billion YTD in repurchases and have $15 billion dry powder for M&A in payments or wealth tuck-ins. Dividend up to $1.20/share, targeting 15-18% ROE through cycle while maintaining strong capital.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Tom Lee:
How are you managing interest rate risk and asset sensitivity?

David Patel:
Good question, Tom. We're asset-sensitive +$285 million for +100 bps, with swaps hedging $15 billion notional to close duration gap. EVE within tolerances, stress-tested for cuts or hikes. Regional strategies like euro swaptions and deposit innovations keep us resilient, NII guide $29-30 billion FY24.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Karen Brown with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Karen Brown:
Can you discuss the performance of your commercial loan segment?

Lisa Wong:
Sure, Karen. Commercial loans grew 9.1% YoY to $148 billion, led by 12% C&I on healthcare/manufacturing capex and 14% multifamily. Quality strong at 0.75% NPLs, AI underwriting speeds approvals 30%, low CRE office exposure. Cross-sell boosting fees 18%.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Mike Chen for any closing remarks.

Mike Chen:
Thank you for your interest in GlobalBank Holdings. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
